presentations.title: ADV-01: Three Threats Are Easier Than Two
presentations.subtitle: Peak Concurrency vs Release Scheduling
presentations.description: Room A has 3 enemies and peak K=3 concurrency, but generous 3.0s deadlines make it 100% solvable (M = +65 tics). Room B has only 2 enemies, but tight 0.30s deadlines create an unavoidable deadline breach (M = -29 tics).
presentations.takeaway: Threat count is not workload. Timing is.

presentations.title: ADV-02: Same Room, Different Route
presentations.subtitle: Clearability Is Trajectory-Conditioned
presentations.description: The exact same room geometry produces opposite tactical outcomes depending on movement path. A direct rush exposes the player to simultaneous crossfires, while a methodical flank route staggers sightlines into sequential 1v1 duels.
presentations.takeaway: A map is not tactically good or bad in isolation; clearability is a property of the path.

presentations.title: ADV-03: Global vs Local Tactical MRI
presentations.subtitle: Whole-Route Optimum vs Local Approach Choke
presentations.description: On Dust II A-Long, an aggressive wide swing looks deceptively superior on whole-route score (M=+2) due to shorter total travel time, but harbors a fatal local crossfire at the corner. Suffix Tactical Margin isolates the acute danger zone.
presentations.takeaway: A route can look safe overall while hiding an unserviceable local choke.

presentations.title: ADV-04: Causal Repair Microscope
presentations.subtitle: Sub-Meter Geometric Edit Restores Positive Margin
presentations.description: Sliding a single partition by +1.10 m delays Threat 2's un-occlusion timestamp by 8 tics, transforming an unserviceable -6 tic failure into a +2 tic (+57 ms) safety reserve.
presentations.takeaway: Obstacle +1.10 m → Delayed Reveal → Reserve +2 tics

presentations.title: ADV-05: The Quantization Staircase
presentations.subtitle: Continuous Geometry vs Discrete Clock Thresholds
presentations.source_fixture: F06 Wall Perturbation & Ascent Pitch Sweep
presentations.description: Continuous obstacle shifts move reveal timestamps continuously, but Tactical Margin changes in discrete integer steps on the 35-Hz game clock. Angular pitch changes within a single aim-slew bucket produce zero discrete difference.
presentations.takeaway: Continuous geometric changes only alter clearability when crossing discrete simulation clock boundaries.

presentations.title: ADV-06: The Model Says No
presentations.subtitle: Falsifiability on Unsolvable Dry Chokes
presentations.description: When entering B-Site from Upper Tunnels, simultaneous sightlines cannot be serialized dry by left or right hugging paths (M = -7 tics). The model refuses to fabricate a solution, verifying the necessity of tactical smokes/flashes.
presentations.takeaway: A trustworthy diagnostic tool must be capable of declaring when dry gunplay is physically impossible.

presentations.title: ADV-07: Prediction Meets Execution
presentations.subtitle: Discrete Schedulers Executed by 3D Controllers
presentations.description: A 35-Hz 3D controller rotates along unit-sphere S^2 geodesic arcs using Slerp. Physical execution events match the discrete scheduler's predicted completion tics with exact bit-for-bit parity.
presentations.takeaway: Tactical Margin is an executable contract: t_j(event) ≡ C_j - 1.

presentations.title: ADV-08: Source Success, Engine Failure
presentations.subtitle: Visualizing External Engine Transfer Residuals
presentations.source_fixture: Family 1 vs Family 4 ViZDoom Transfer Gaps
presentations.description: 80% of unserviceable layouts were repaired in the source model, and 75% survived in native C++ ViZDoom. Transfer gaps are caused by engine line-of-sight rasterization, collision bounding boxes, and coordinate quantization.
presentations.takeaway: Mathematical correctness requires an empirical deployment guard band when exported to third-party game engines.
